transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Trips to Kansas and Iowa
are back on President Trump's weekend schedule.
They're two of the states where Republicans
are in competitive congressional races
in the run-up to November 3rd.
The University of Florida Election Lab says so far,
more than 45 million people have voted early.
And today, the administration suffered a legal setback
in its intensified scrutiny of local elections.
The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals rejected
a Justice Department request for California
to set aside disputed ballots received in the midterms.
Trump is also alleging fraud in the Senate race in Alaska,
where there are two Dan Sullivan's on the Senate ballot,
one of whom is the Republican incumbent.
Democratic candidate Mary Peltola is denying
a New York Times report alleging she knew
about the ballot-stacking scheme
to confuse voters in her favor.
I knew nothing about any other candidates
on the ballot except for me and the incumbent.
This was the final day of trading for the month,
and investors are dumping tech shares
with Amazon and Alphabet earnings,
fueling doubts about massive investments in AI.
The Nasdaq-composited closed down more than 700 points,
or roughly 2.8%.
David Wessel is director of the Hutchins Center
on Fiscal and Monetary Policy at the Brookings Institution.
It's down 10% from its October 6th high.
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange,
suffered a cyber heist with hackers
stealing more than $6 billion in cryptocurrencies.
Here's NPR's Rafael Naum.
It's the biggest crypto heist in history,
far surpassing the $1.6 billion
that was stolen from a smaller exchange, Bybit, in 2025.
A lot is unknown about how exactly it happened.
But so far, Binance and researchers that are looking
into this say hackers accessed the trading accounts
of customers of the exchange
and effectively stole their cryptocurrencies.
A prominent crypto research firm called TRM
said it's highly confident a North Korean hacking group
may be behind the cyber heist.
Binance has promised to cover all losses
suffered by customers.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
Parade celebrating Milwaukee's first
Major League Baseball Championship in 69 years
brought tens of thousands of people
to the city's downtown today.
Here's Chuck Kurnbach.
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays
in the World Series this week.
Brewers fans at the parade cheered their heroes on
as the players went by on platforms atop buses.
43-year-old Alvaro Aleman says he just had to be on hand.
Oh my God, I've been waiting for this my entire life.
I've been waiting for this my entire life
to see World Series champion.
It's the Brewers first championship
joining the Milwaukee Braves
who won the World Series in 1957.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kurnbach in Milwaukee.
This is NPR News.
Pope Leo the 14th confirms he voted
in the US midterm elections casting a mail-in ballot
in Chicago.
Megan Williams has more from Rome.
The Vatican says the Pope has exercised his right
to vote as an American citizen whenever he's been eligible.
It also confirms he voted during his years living in Peru
where he qualified to take part in elections there.
The statement emphasizes the Pope's belief
that participating in democracy is both a right
and a duty for citizens.
Leo's vote is a reminder that along with his role
as head of the Catholic Church,
he retains his US citizenship and exercises his rights.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
As gasoline remains a buck 20 higher than a year ago
and as diesel hovers around $6.30,
major oil companies ExxonMobil, Chevron and Shell
reported soaring profits this quarter.
NPR's Will Aruban listened to the company's earnings calls.
Exxon doubled its earnings compared to this time last year.
Shell's earnings nearly doubled.
Chevron's were up 180%.
Together, the company's earned
just over $36 billion this quarter.
All kinds of oil products have gotten pricier this year.
Due to the war in Iran,
less oil has been getting out of the Middle East
and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries
have especially hampered the global diesel supply.
The oil companies gave some of their earnings
to shareholders through dividends,
but for the most part, they're in a wait and see stance.
Will Aruban, NPR News, this is NPR.

topics.text: Trump's weekend schedule adds trips to Kansas and Iowa, competitive House states
Florida Election Lab reports over 45 million people have already voted early
Ninth Circuit rejects Justice Department request to set aside disputed California midterm ballots
Trump alleges fraud in Alaska Senate race; Mary Peltola denies knowing about ballot-stacking scheme
Nasdaq closes down about 2.8% as investors dump tech shares after Amazon and Alphabet earnings
Binance suffers crypto cyber heist of more than $6 billion, likely by North Korean hackers
Milwaukee holds downtown parade for Brewers' first World Series title in 69 years
Pope Leo XIV confirms he cast a mail-in ballot in the US midterms from Chicago
ExxonMobil, Chevron and Shell report soaring quarterly profits amid high fuel prices
